title: Add manager-side Reset PRDs action that archives current PRD and resets repo autonomy state
specification:
# PRD: Add manager-side Reset PRDs action that archives current PRD and resets repo autonomy state

Priority: high

## Problem
Managers need a safe way to abandon a stuck or unwanted in-flight PRD and return a repo to a fresh autonomy state. The current system only archives completed PRDs and exposes no manager-side reset/archive action for active work.

## Goal
Provide a manager-side control that archives the current PRD as reset/abandoned, clears active autonomy execution state for the repo, and leaves the control plane in a clean idle state with preserved history.

## Requirements
- Add a manager-side `Reset PRDs` action for each repo in the control plane.
- Require explicit confirmation that names the PRD being reset and warns that active implementation/review work will be interrupted.
- Create backend/API support for a reset action; current control-plane routes do not expose this operation.
- Archive the active PRD into history with a distinct reset/abandoned status or reason instead of marking it completed.
- Clear repo-local active/queued PRD execution state so the repo returns to a fresh idle state.
- Handle running agent/review activity safely so live tasks are stopped or detached consistently rather than silently orphaned.
- Keep an audit trail visible in PRD History, including reset timestamp and reason if provided.
- Refresh manager/project status views immediately after reset so no stale active PRD remains visible.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A manager can trigger `Reset PRDs` from the control plane for a repo with an active PRD.
- After confirmation, the repo shows no active PRD, no queued PRDs tied to the reset run, and autonomy status returns to an idle/fresh state.
- The reset PRD appears in History with a clear reset/abandoned label and preserved PRD details.
- If implementation or review workers were active, the UI no longer shows them attached to the reset PRD after the operation completes.
- The operation is not reported as a completed PRD archive; it is distinguishable from normal completion.
- If no active PRD exists, the action is disabled or returns a clear no-op message.

## Verification
- Add unit coverage for reset state transitions, including active PRD, queued PRD, and no-active-PRD cases.
- Add API tests for the new reset endpoint, including confirmation validation and post-reset status shape.
- Add control-plane UI coverage for button visibility, confirmation flow, and post-reset refresh.
- Manually verify on a repo with an active PRD and active reviewer/implementation tasks that reset removes the PRD from active status and records it in History with reset metadata.
